newsitem.title: CANADA: United Grain says bid not good for farmers.
newsitem.headline: United Grain says bid not good for farmers.

text.p: The chairman of United Grain Growers Ltd said on Sunday that a Saturday vote by member delegates from the Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators in favor of a C$172 million takeover bid for UGG is not in the best interests of farmers in Western Canada.

"The Pools' management indicated they had persuaded their delegates to take this step well before they announced their bid on February 20, so this is not a surprise," UGG chairman Theodore Allen said in a statement. "But it is disappointing that the delegates could support the bid and ignore what we believe is best for the farming community."
Allen advised United Grain shareholders to take a "wait and see" approach to the C$13.75 a share takeover offer from the Pools.

"The Pools' management may have convinced delegates to pursue this potentially damaging course, but they are a long way from persuading UGG shareholders to tender to their inadequate bid," Allen said.
He said the bid threatens to seriously lessen competition in the grain handling industry.
"Our customers and farmer shareholders are telling us they don't want to lose their choice of service," he said.

"UGG believes farmers all across the West should consider the impact on them if the Pools were to be allowed to gain control of more than 70 percent of the grain handling and storage capacity in both Manitoba and Alberta."

Allen said the cost of the takeover would place the Pools under a heavy financial burden, raising concerns that do nothave the financial strength to pay for the capital improvements their operations need and the more than C$172 million it would cost to buy United Grain.
"At least one credit rating agency has already expressed concern about the Pools' long-term financial outlook."

Alberta Wheat Pool Chief Financial Officer Geoffrey Southwood said on Saturday that delegates voted 98 percent in favor of the takeover bid for United Grain and that only a few conditions to the offer remain in effect, such as the waiving of a poison pill plan, which UGG adopted on February 14.
The Pools will challenge United Grain's poison pill plan at a March 11-12 hearing in the Manitoba Court of Queen's Bench.

The plan is triggered once any investor has more than 15 percent of United Grain's stock. United Grain said last week that the pill was triggered after the Pools raised their stake in UGG to 14.98 percent and acquired an irrevocable lock-up agreement with a group of shareholders holding 6.4 percent of UGG's stock.

It said the pill will take effect March 4. At that time UGG shareholders, except the Pools will have the right to buy up to 8.5 more shares at C$5.88. AWP and MWP raised their stake in United Grain to 14.98 percent on February 13 and announced their takeover bid.

The Pools said that UGG shareholders can tender their shares prior to the expiry of the offer on March 27, 1997. The Pools' offer of $13.75 per share represents a 34 percent premium over the average closing price for the 10 trading days prior to the date the Pools commenced making significant market purchases.
Last week United Grain shares were trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange around C$14.15 a share.
